## Overview

LRPBX103 is the **wide-delta prior-sensitivity companion** to
[LRPBX03](../lrp-rli-bx-003/). It is the same staggered block-active exposure model, the
same data and the same sampler settings, differing in exactly one thing: the prior on
the focal exposure effect.

| | LRPBX03 (reference) | LRPBX103 (this model) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| exposure effect $\delta$ | $\mathcal{N}(0,\ 0.3)$ (distal tier) | $\mathcal{N}(0,\ 0.5)$ |
| everything else | — | identical |

## Why this model exists

The distal-tier tightening (#141) prices broad standardised-transfer outcomes at
$\tau \sim \mathcal{N}(0, 0.3)$, and UE2 is distal. The prior-critical review (#382,
recommendation 4) asks for a single $\mathcal{N}(0, 0.5)$ check on the distal tier to
confirm the tightening is not attenuating a real transfer effect. The ITT distal
outcomes (R/E/UR/UE/T/F) are certified by the standard 44-cell treatment-prior sweep,
and the aligned family's cohort contrast was never tiered — which leaves this
block-exposure comparator as the one distal focal term without sensitivity evidence.

If the reference $\delta$ is genuinely data-dominated, the posterior here should match
it to within Monte-Carlo error; a materially larger effect under the wider prior would
mean the distal scale is attenuating a real transfer signal.

_Reading rules as LRPBX03:_ block 2 has no t1 baseline and no randomised contrast, so
$\delta$ is an **adjusted association** under either prior. These words were not
taught, so an effect ≈ 0 is the expected fidelity result, not a power failure.
